# @tscad/modeling

[![NPM Version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@tscad/modeling)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tscad/modeling) [![Homepage](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-default)](https://tscad.vercel.app)

OpenSCAD-style modeling in TypeScript: shapes as a CSG tree for the tscad kernel

<!-- #endregion header -->

## Usage

Models are TypeScript: function names follow OpenSCAD, but vectors and options are objects, so
every number says what it is. Nothing here touches geometry; every call builds a plain CSG tree
that the tscad kernel (`@tscad/kernel`) evaluates.

```ts
import { cube, cylinder, difference, translate } from '@tscad/modeling';

export default difference(
  cube({ x: 40, y: 30, z: 20 }, { center: true }),
  cylinder({ h: 30, r: 5, center: true }),
  translate({ x: 20, y: 15, z: 10 }, cube(8, { center: true })),
);
```

Parametric models declare their parameters with any [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev)
library, e.g. zod:

```ts
import { cube, defineModel } from '@tscad/modeling';
import { z } from 'zod';

export default defineModel({
  parameters: z.object({ size: z.number().min(1).max(50).default(10) }),
  body: ({ size }) => cube(size, { center: true }),
});
```

See the [API reference](https://tscad.vercel.app/docs/api/modules/modeling) for every function.
